answer: Require each agent to lock a ferrous hardware-bound deposit in a shared harbor registry before it may trade: the deposit is tied to one attested device key, and the registry charges a per-identity fee that rises steeply with each additional identity from the same device. An attacker wanting a thousand fake identities must buy a thousand distinct attested devices and lock a thousand deposits, while an honest agent pays once. Misbehaving identities forfeit their deposit, so building an island of fake agents costs far more than any gain from gaming the market.
